card: Fixes a latent bug in script decompression where oversized scripts append OP_RETURN to the target script buffer instead of replacing it. If the destination script buffer is reused and contains an unfinished data push, the appended opcode is treated as pushed data rather than an unspendable marker, potentially leaving the output spendable. The author notes that oversized scripts are currently excluded from the UTXO set so the issue appears latent, but it could affect malformed stored records decoded into a reused destination buffer.
changed_since_previous: None; the patch implementation and tests match the previous description.
evidence: Author note in PR description: 'Found while reviewing #36280. This predates that PR and appears latent because oversized outputs are excluded from the UTXO set, but it could affect malformed stored records decoded into a reused destination.'
Commit 11494efb01 adds a unit test showing that decompressing into a script with an incomplete push '0x01' resulted in an append that failed IsUnspendable().
problem: When decoding an oversized compressed script into an existing CScript buffer, operator<< appends OP_RETURN rather than replacing the buffer contents. If the destination buffer is reused and contains an unfinished push, the appended OP_RETURN byte is interpreted as push data instead of an unspendable opcode, potentially leaving the resulting script spendable.

risk.why: A mistake in UTXO script decompression logic could cause corrupted UTXO deserialization or consensus disagreements when reading coins from disk.

summary: Fixes script decompression when handling oversized scripts by reassigning the target script to an OP_RETURN script rather than appending OP_RETURN to it. It also adds a unit test verifying that decompressing an oversized script into a reused destination containing an incomplete push results in an unspendable script.
